BiblicalUsage: Backwards — achoranniyth describes walking with your face turned away. Shem and Japheth "went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father," refusing to look on Noah's shame; and Eli, when he heard the ark was taken, "fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died." One backward step covers shame; the other ends a life.
TheologicalSignificance: Walking backwards is a posture, not a doctrine, and the two scenes it describes — covering shame in honour, and falling in judgment — carry whatever lesson there is.
